title: Cogolin, crafts, carpets, pipes and the old town
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: Cogolin is not only a transition point between plain and sea. The town keeps a strong craft memory that remains visible in its streets, squares and local identity.
content:
Cogolin is often approached through its access roads or its openings towards the marinas. Yet the old town remains the best way to understand what shapes the commune: a history of making, local trade and year-round life.

A working town before a mere stop

Carpets and pipes long carried the name of Cogolin beyond the gulf. This craft memory is not marginal. It still explains part of the tone of the centre, more inhabited, more made and less purely seaside than in other communes.

The old streets keep that density

In the old town, small squares, fountains, narrow passages and stone facades recall a commune where people produced, exchanged and truly lived. The walk gains depth when it shows these traces instead of hurrying only towards the maritime outlet.

Why this angle completes the visit

Understanding craft traditions changes the interpretation of Cogolin. One is no longer crossing only a transition commune; one is entering a town whose personality was also built through workshop life, manual skill and local continuity.
